title: Chapter 2: The Investor and Inflation; Zweig commentary

claims.text: A stock cannot be preferable to a bond at every purchase price and yield; inflation exposure must be evaluated together with valuation, liabilities and the investor's horizon.

Nominal profit can coexist with a purchasing-power loss. Compare real as well as nominal outcomes, using an explicit measured inflation series and compatible time intervals rather than the book's dated numerical assumptions.
claims.anchor: how much you keep after inflation

claims.text: Stocks are an imperfect inflation hedge: the commentary reports inflation shortfalls in some overlapping five-year windows, and short/intermediate drawdowns can affect an investor before any long-run protection materializes.

Reject the statement that inflation can raise stock values only by raising the rate of earnings on capital as a complete valuation identity; changing nominal earnings, discount rates, accounting measurements and repricing complicate that inference.

Inflation-linked bonds and property exposure are mechanisms to investigate, not universally safe substitutes for cash. Zweig's own warning about short-run TIPS volatility limits the surrounding absolute-safety language; tax, legal and product examples remain dated.

assimilation: Extend the value framework from quoted dollars to purchasing power and timing of liabilities. Refuse to infer an all-stock allocation merely from an inflation forecast. A business's pricing power, reinvestment needs and financing burden matter separately from a generic equity label. Keep inflation-linked contracts and real assets outside the VTI-only pilot's allowed actions unless a later policy explicitly expands scope.
adversarial_review: The historical tables use different capital/profit measures and overlapping windows, not independent causal experiments. Graham's prospective 3% inflation and 8% stock-return illustrations were explicitly uncertain and must not become current inputs. The chart orders years by inflation rather than time, so it cannot be read as a chronological strategy. Claims about gold ownership law, taxation, utilities and particular funds require fresh primary verification before operational use. Contractual inflation adjustment does not guarantee a bond fund's market value or match every household's personal inflation.
memory_delta: Separate nominal and real results, inspect inflation pass-through and capital intensity, and preserve near-term liquidity needs. Treat stocks and TIPS as conditional risk exposures rather than complete inflation insurance; no fixed current inflation forecast is learned.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 57-70; rendered tables 2-1/2-2 and figure 2-1. Table/figure measures and historical ordering were checked, not reused as current forecasts.
